lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put experience in reverse chronological order, with Harbor Payments above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: Harbor ended more recently than Crestline.

items.says: Explain the transition from the MBA and product internship to diesel mechanic work.
items.because: Recruiters may wonder whether you are still pursuing product roles.

items.says: Consider placing the food-rescue venture before less relevant professional experience.
items.because: It is highly relevant to product roles.

items.says: Use one date style with en dashes throughout.
Use numerals consistently or follow one rule for small numbers.
Check that the LinkedIn URL is active and matches the résumé’s dates and titles.
Consider a portfolio if it contains substantive product artifacts or case studies.
Confirm that June 2025 is the actual MBA degree-conferral date.
items.because: That date has passed.

items.says: Add a concentration, honors, or relevant coursework only if it supports product candidacy.
Give context for how the mechanic role fits the product or operations direction.
Emphasize transferable elements rather than purely technical maintenance tasks.
Use present tense for ongoing responsibilities and past tense for completed projects.
Clarify whether five days is an average, maximum, or service target.
Support the implication that your work maintained the turnaround time.
items.because: The work may have merely occurred within that time.

items.says: Add reliability, cost, or return-to-service impact if possible.
items.because: Turnaround time does not show whether the repairs were durable.

items.says: Add the scale, frequency, inspection outcome, or operational impact of the winch work.
Show whether the service records improved compliance or inspection readiness.
items.because: “Logged service records” sounds administrative without that evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether the fleet passed inspections, avoided findings, or reduced downtime.
Add a promotion or title progression if one occurred.
items.because: The role spans five years.

items.says: Identify the scorecard metrics, coverage, and decisions enabled.
Make your role in the monthly review meeting more specific.
items.because: “The monthly review meeting that discussed them” is vague and undersells your role.

items.says: Add a carrier, service, cost, or escalation outcome, or consider removing the bullet.
items.because: Without a measurable result, it is the weakest Crestline bullet.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% reduction is relative and give its baseline or measurement period.
Say whether the improvement was sustained after retraining.
Specify the forecast-error measure.
items.because: Forecast error can be calculated in multiple ways.

items.says: Clarify the business scope of the S&OP work.
items.because: The reader needs to understand its scale.

items.says: Use consistent serial commas in the list of functions.
Split or shorten the bullet’s several accomplishments.
items.because: It combines deployment, documentation, training, negotiation, and labor savings.

items.says: Prioritize rollout, adoption, workflow change, and training over negotiations for product roles.
items.because: Those elements are more relevant to the target role.

items.says: Replace or remove “taking over.”
items.because: It emphasizes task ownership rather than accomplishment.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 annual hours were measured or calculated.
Add adoption, route-efficiency, service, or financial impact if available.
Quantify any savings from vendor negotiation separately.
items.because: Otherwise the negotiation remains an unsupported activity.

items.says: Give the product internship stronger visual and content emphasis.
items.because: It is the most directly relevant product experience.

items.says: Reduce the six bullets for this three-month internship.
items.because: Several overlap.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period and whether the result came from an experiment, pilot, or before-and-after analysis.
Add a verification, fraud, abandonment, or compliance guardrail if one was monitored.
items.because: Reducing verification steps can raise risk questions.

items.says: Clarify that the 2,300 merchants were the measured population, if so.
items.because: They should not be confused with the eventual rollout population.

items.says: State the conversion result consistently as a percentage-point lift or a correctly calculated relative increase.
items.because: The two should not be alternated without distinction.

items.says: Add statistical confidence, test duration, or a major guardrail if concise and accurate.
Confirm that the rollout really reached “all merchants.”
items.because: It may have covered only a region, segment, or eligible group.

items.says: Defining RICE Reach as support tickets a feature would close is inconsistent with the framework.
items.because: Reach usually counts users, accounts, or events affected in a defined period; closed tickets are closer to an outcome or impact proxy.

items.says: If retaining RICE, show that all four dimensions were applied and influenced a decision.
Do not rely on naming the framework as the accomplishment.
items.because: Framework terminology alone does not demonstrate judgment or impact.

items.says: Fix the introductory phrase so it identifies the actor cleanly.
items.because: The current sentence structure does not.

items.says: Specify the roadmap decision and the result, approval, or resource allocation that followed.
Combine this with the preceding roadmap bullet or keep the stronger one.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: The checkout A/B-test bullet duplicates the earlier conversion result.
Session-level randomization does not automatically establish an effect on individual customers.
items.because: It supports an estimate of session conversion, and repeat sessions from one customer can create dependence.

items.says: Clarify whether this is the same onboarding initiative as the first internship bullet.
items.because: Repeating the story should add new information.

items.says: Add the size or expected impact of the two-region expansion if known.
Focus on the decision secured rather than the act of presenting.
Clarify whether the student venture is an active business, school project, or volunteer initiative.
items.because: Recruiters may still want to understand its status.

items.says: Include recent results for the ongoing venture.
items.because: The bullets rely on first-year metrics.

items.says: Explain how the nine tonnes were measured and what the figure represents.
items.because: It could mean food collected, redistributed, or estimated waste avoided.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students were actual users.
items.because: The figure could instead be the eligible campus population.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Give the period over which weekly active users increased.
Clarify whether interviews alone led to reminders or other evidence also informed the decision.
Avoid implying reminders definitively caused the increase if other changes were not controlled for.
items.because: The reminders may not have been experimentally tested.

items.says: Ensure the definition of an active user is consistent and meaningful.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 26.7%.

items.says: Give the fill-rate measurement period and say whether the result was sustained.
Explain how volunteer shifts affected slot availability or fulfillment.
items.because: The causal connection is not immediately obvious.

items.says: Connect the operational result to marketplace supply, service reliability, or user experience.
items.because: The bullet reads more like operational execution than software product work.

items.says: Clarify team size if you led the practicum team.
Use “savings” rather than “saving” for the projected cost reductions.
items.because: The plural is the grammatically standard form.

items.says: Clarify whether $2.4M is gross savings, net savings, or an opportunity estimate.
Give the model’s major basis or assumptions if they establish credibility.
Replace the passive construction with active ownership.
Quantify the intake changes or their effect on time, errors, or staff effort.
Specify adoption rate, timing, or operational result.
items.because: “Adopted by front-desk staff” is weak without them.

items.says: Clarify your contribution versus the team’s contribution.
The pilot-approval outcome duplicates the first practicum bullet.
items.because: Two bullets on approval leave less room for analysis and process-redesign detail.

items.says: If retaining this bullet, clarify your role in the presentation and whether the pilot launched or was measured.
List only skills demonstrated elsewhere in the résumé.
Reconsider A/B testing until the session-level versus customer-level issue is corrected.
items.because: You should be comfortable explaining experimental design, significance, power, and guardrails.

items.says: Make “requirements writing” more specific.
items.because: Skills sections work better with recognizable, defensible capabilities.

items.says: Strengthen the sparse tools list with relevant tools you can genuinely use.
items.because: Many product roles expect capabilities such as SQL, BI, prototyping, design, or documentation.

items.says: Show advanced Excel capability through experience evidence if applicable.
items.because: A proficiency label alone is unsupported.

items.says: Tie Amplitude to an accomplishment or project if it was used meaningfully.
items.because: Otherwise it may look like keyword padding.

items.says: Omit basic office tools unless they are relevant to the job description.
